\[
\hat{x} = y + f_\theta(y),\qquad
\operatorname{Attention}(Q, K, V) = V \cdot \operatorname{SoftMax}\!\left(\frac{K^{\top} Q}{\alpha}\right)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(y\): The degraded image
- \(f_\theta\): The network with its trained weights
- \(Q, K, V\): Queries, keys and values, one row per pixel
- \(\alpha\): A learned temperature
- \(\hat{x}\): The restored image

y is the degraded image and f the network, which predicts a correction. Q, K and V come from the features by 1 x 1 and depthwise 3 x 3 convolutions, and have one row per pixel and one column per channel. K transposed times Q is a channel by channel matrix. So the attention compares channels across the whole image, and its cost grows linearly with the number of pixels. alpha is a learned temperature. The network has four levels, each halving the size, and a gated feed-forward part in every block.
